text:
alec: Hey team — our GitHub Actions job using the quickstart-ci example suddenly started failing on the first API call with 403. Local dev works fine. CI logs show auth refresh attempts and then a 429 rate limit. Anyone seen CI-only failures like this? :confused:

devex-bot: Ticket created DEVEX-5510. Please paste the relevant CI logs and how the key is configured (repo secret, org key, service account).

alec: We're injecting REDWOOD_API_KEY as a repo secret (the workspace service key that infra team gave us). Snippet from GH Actions step logs:
```
Running quickstart CI script
[2026-03-23T07:12:01Z] auth: lookup cached token -> none
[2026-03-23T07:12:01Z] auth: refresh -> POST /auth/refresh
[2026-03-23T07:12:02Z] http: 403 Forbidden from auth/refresh
Error: refresh rejected: 403
[2026-03-23T07:12:02Z] auth: retry refresh (1/3)
[2026-03-23T07:12:03Z] http: 403 Forbidden from auth/refresh
[2026-03-23T07:12:03Z] auth: retry refresh (2/3)
[2026-03-23T07:12:04Z] http: 403 Forbidden from auth/refresh
[2026-03-23T07:12:04Z] http: 429 Too Many Requests
Action failed with exit code 1
```

nora: Two things here. 1) Workspace/service keys often require an org header when used from untrusted runtimes (CI is untrusted like the browser). 2) The SDK retrying the refresh aggressively can cause a 429 when the gate is intentional (billing/terms or server policy). In CI you usually want a clear immediate failure and a hint, not multiple refresh retries.

paul: Also, CLI login isn't an option for CI. For automation we recommend either: a) a dedicated CI service key that is allowed by the org (admin-created and permitted for automation), or b) a personal API key stored as a secret for non-production tests. If the org has billing/terms pending, those keys might still be subject to first-call gating.

alec: How do we check if it's billing gating vs workspace key header requirement? In this case the org admin says billing is enabled.

nora: Quick debug: 1) try replacing the secret with a personal API key (Profile -> API keys) in the job — if that works, it's an org-gating or header issue. 2) If personal key works, create a CI-specific key via console and mark it as automation-friendly. 3) Inspect the API response body from the 403; when it's billing-gated we return a short message like "first-call blocked: billing/terms required" (although SDK might be hiding it). In CI capture the raw HTTP response.

ci-bot: Note: For security, do not paste full keys in chat. Use masking when you share logs.

alec: Replaced with a personal key in the secret — CI job passed immediately. So it's tied to the workspace/service key semantics.

paul: OK — follow-ups: - We'll update quickstart-ci README to call out that repo secrets should use personal/CI-specific keys, and that workspace keys are server-only and may require a proxy/extra header. - SDK change: when refresh returns 403 and there's no cached token, do not retry aggressively in non-interactive environments; surface a typed error like `ERR_AUTOMATION_GATE` with a human hint URL. - Console improvement: allow creating "CI tokens" explicitly flagged for automation that bypass certain untrusted runtime checks (audit trail + TTL).

nora: I'll add DEVEX-5510 tasks: quickstart README edit, SDK retry policy tweak, and a console UX ticket for CI tokens. Also propose adding a small snippet to the quickstart-ci YAML demonstrating how to set a personal key as a secret and a link to the automation key docs.

alec: Thanks — that will save other teams. I'll attach the GH Actions repro to the ticket and sandbox a CI token request with our infra team.
